items.title: Insurer Sanctioned Over Serious Breaches
items.teaser: A life insurer being sanction by the Life Code Compliance Committee after more than 10,000 breaches drew much reader interest this week… A life insurer has been sanctioned by the Life Insurance Code Compliance Committee after more than 10,000 breaches meant customers received annual notices that were inaccurate…

items.title: Anti-hawking laws pose potential threat to common referral practices
items.teaser: A core part of Financial Services Minister Dan Mulino’s tranche of reforms announced last month was a new anti-hawking regime, which will enhance consent requirements, limit the existing financial advice exemption to existing client relationships and strengthen penalties for breaches.

items.title: Why wasn’t Garry Crole permanently banned?
items.teaser: Effective from 4 September, Garry Crole was banned from performing as a director or responsible manager or any function involved in carrying on a financial services business, which ASIC said was a result of concerns related to his former roles as director and responsible manager of InterPrac Financial Planning.

items.title: ART reviews five-year bans of two former advisers
items.teaser: Two former financial advisers have had their bannings reviewed by the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART) over participating in flawed advice models.

items.title: Review tribunal upholds Venture Egg, FSGA adviser bans
items.teaser: Shane Monte Silva, formerly an authorised representative of FSGA and financial adviser at AS Financial Planning Pty Ltd, was initially banned by the regulator on 10 December 2025 after finding he had contravened financial services laws when providing superannuation switching advice to five clients.

items.title: Tribunal affirms ASIC ban on advisers at the centre of Shield and First Guardian failed advice
items.teaser: The Administrative Review Tribunal has affirmed the five-year bans imposed by ASIC on financial advisers Andrew Hanley and Shane Monte Silva for their role in switching clients’ superannuation to Shield and First Guardian without proper assessment.

items.title: Victims’ advocate says Crole banning ‘best thing ASIC has done’
items.teaser: A leading advocate for investors in the collapsed Shield and First Guardian master funds has welcomed the banning of the former chief executive of the licensee at the centre of investor losses.

items.title: Planned new home builds will be cancelled
items.teaser: Hogan said off-the-plan apartment projects depend on SMSF buyers for early presales and without them, developers won’t get finance and the homes will never be built. “Labor has banned self-managed super funds from borrowing to buy residential property, including new builds.

items.title: Tribunal affirms InterPrac, FSGA adviser bans
items.teaser: The Administrative Review Tribunal has affirmed ASIC's decisions to ban two former financial advisers from InterPrac Financial Planning and Financial Services Group Australia (FSGA) who were involved in the Shield and First Guardian master funds for five years.

items.title: FAAA warns CSLR bill could hit before Christmas
items.teaser: Already this year, CSLR costs have skyrocketed.

items.title: Treasury floats innovative businesses CGT concession draft laws
items.teaser: Treasury has released draft legislation on a capital gains tax (CGT) concession for start-ups and small businesses, embedding several amendments that have been lauded as a "substantial win" by an industry body.

items.title: ART upholds ban on former financial advisers
items.teaser: ART found that Andrew Hanley and Shane Monte Silva participated in flawed advice models that failed to place clients’ interests first and resulted in inappropriate superannuation switching advice.

items.title: APRA simplifies retirement data collection by trustees
items.teaser: As part of its response to industry feedback on the proposed Retirement Reporting Framework, the prudential regulator has streamlined data requirements, ensuring transparency while reducing the excessive data collection burden.

items.title: AFSLs reminded over accurate reports after PI questioning
items.teaser: An ASIC review of AFSLs and their professional indemnity insurance (PI) found only one AFSL held inadequate PI, requiring a breach report to be submitted. The regulator’s annual AFSL data collection examined the PI insurance held by licensees, their policy excess and whether they have a claim paid.

items.title: ‘Punitive pricing’ won’t fix the licensee scrutiny gap: Shuttleworth
items.teaser: Centrepoint Alliance chief executive John Shuttleworth says shifting the bulk of funding the ASIC levy from individual advisers to licensees won’t fix the problem it’s designed to address.

items.title: First Super appoints new chief executive
items.teaser: First Super has appointed a new chief executive who was part of LUCRF Super's leadership team for 18 years.

items.title: ‘Doesn’t cut the mustard’: Equity Trustees defends apparent governance breakdown
items.teaser: Appearing before a joint parliamentary committee on 10 September, Michael O’Brien, managing director of Equity Trustees and non-executive director Catherine Robson defended the trustees’ conduct in relation to Shield and First Guardian.

items.title: One Nation ‘super pay boost’ at odds with adequacy, retirement plans
items.teaser: As new research reveals more than a third of Australians want a superannuation retirement balance of $1.25 million or more, One Nation has unveiled a plan to allow workers pocket 3 per cent of their super contributions, which could leave them tens of thousands of dollars short of their target.

items.title: Hewison departure will open door to ‘fresh voice, ideas, enthusiasm’
items.teaser: Second-generation Hewison Private Wealth managing director Andrew Hewison tells Professional Planner there will be no changes to the business and no clients will be affected as a result of Pemba Capital Partners’ investment, followed by his departure at the end of the year.

items.title: Australians aiming for big retirement balances: MLC
items.teaser: This data comes as the rest of the retirement and super sector tries lift confidence amid growing anxiety within the market and Australia faces down a ‘Silver Tsunami’ of retirees.

items.title: Unisuper deepens advice capabilities with head appointment
items.teaser: This comes as the Government has essentially greenlit the large superfunds too invest deeper in their financial advice capabilities following the announcement of the implementation of the ‘New Class of Adviser’ regime.

items.title: Capital Haus renews Xplan deal as acquisition run continues
items.teaser: Capital Haus has extended its technology agreement with Iress, keeping Xplan as the platform underpinning its advice operations. Xplan has been the platform used by Capital Haus since it operated as a single independent advice practice, according to Iress.

items.title: Lower pension spending should not be the sole measure of retirement success
items.teaser: Richard Webb, CPA Australia Superannuation Lead, said Australia risks focusing too heavily on reducing Age Pension costs rather than ensuring retirees enjoy adequate retirement incomes.

items.title: SMSF record growth highlights appeal of retirement control
items.teaser: The report, released on 8 September, found that there are now 680,301 SMSFs in Australia, with more than 52,000 new entries since June 2025. The June 2026 quarter saw 12,264 new entrants.

items.title: PPS Mutual Appoints Senior BDM in Victoria
items.teaser: PPS Mutual has appointed Voula Makris as Senior Business Development Manager for Victoria, reporting to Shadia Kouzma, the State Manager.

items.title: Russell launches retirement solution
items.teaser: Russell Investments has launched retirement solutions comprising two managed portfolios and a retirement calculator, aimed at helping advisers manage the competing liquidity and growth needs of Australians entering retirement.

items.title: Akumin wants to support ambitious quality firms
items.teaser: Akumin has welcomed firms with as few as two advisers to more than 100 in 2026, CEO Matt Lawler tells Professional Planner that the licensee’s growth strategy is focused on the ambitions and quality of potential target firms, not their size.

items.title: Integro and Coastline merger a vote of confidence in the value of risk advice
items.teaser: The merger of Coastline Private Wealth with fellow WA-based financial advice firm Integro Private Wealth is a vote of confidence by Integro in the value of risk advice, its partner and private wealth adviser Justin Gilmour says.

items.title: TAL Risk Academy Retirement Month Focuses on Advisers’ Role
items.teaser: TAL Risk Academy will run a series of retirement-focused webinars this month to help advisers meet growing demand for trusted guidance before and during retirement.

items.title: Lack of Adviser Support for NCA
items.teaser: Only one in four of those taking our latest poll (25%) support the announcement that the yet-to-be-legislated new class of adviser will initially be limited to life companies and super funds. Two in three (67%) do not support this move, with the rest unsure.

items.title: Significant Changes to Pricing of Advice – Report
items.teaser: Fixed advice fees have replaced models that include asset-based fees as the most common pricing model for ongoing service, reflecting the profession’s increasing focus on non-investment related matters such as guiding clients through challenging situations and helping them avoid costly mistakes, according to new…

items.title: Liquidity divide: Why retirees hold back from guaranteed income
items.teaser: The 2026 AMP Retirement Confidence Pulse found 84 per cent of Australians said guaranteed income for life would help them spend more confidently in retirement but uptake isn’t matching that.

items.title: TIP partners with UNSW to build investment research edge
items.teaser: Teaminvest Private Group (TIP) is partnering with the University of New South Wales (UNSW) to create an investment research platform. TIP and the UNSW Business School have partnered to start the ‘Investment Intelligence and Decision Lab’ (the Lab) which TIP says will boost its intellectual property over time.

items.title: Chalmers puts super at forefront of next election
items.teaser: In a speech to the Super Members Council on Wednesday, Chalmers gave a glimpse of the latest Intergeneration Report findings and said superannuation is a “broader antidote” to the serious intergenerational pressures facing Australia.

items.title: Asset-based fees dwindle as firms price for complexity, not wealth
items.teaser: New research has found that the shift away from asset-based fees is gathering pace, with advice fees increasingly being based on the complexity of the client, not on portfolio size.

items.title: Competence, judgement, diligence the minimum required of licensees
items.teaser: ASIC's finding that former InterPrac boss Garry Crole was neither fit and proper nor competent, and lacked diligence and judgement, is a timely warning: licensee leadership isn't always what advisers assume.

items.title: Opposition and peak SMSF body call for a stop to tinkering with rules
items.teaser: Four substantive changes in just five months has led the Shadow Minister for Financial Services Kevin Hogan to call on the government to quit tinkering with the rules. His plea for greater stability and certainty is supported by the peak SMSF industry body.

items.title: Do It, Delegate It or Dump It
items.teaser: Advisers struggling to find enough hours in the day might benefit from asking a simple question about every task they perform: Should I do it, delegate it or dump it?

items.title: AI boom to drive long-term growth, but it won’t be linear
items.teaser: AI-related technology stocks have enjoyed a meteoric rise over the past three and half years, leading to questions about the sustainability of the AI cycle and the best way for investors to tap into the growth opportunity.

items.title: Nasdaq leadership enters its next phase
items.teaser: AI-led earnings growth and a historic investment cycle continue to place the Nasdaq’s largest companies at the centre of global equity markets.

items.title: Investors price more risk into listed private credit trusts: Morningstar
items.teaser: Investors are pricing in more risk for listed private credit vehicles, which are structured as listed investment trusts (LITs), with some trusts trading at a discount of 25% of their net asset value (NAV), according to Morningstar.

items.title: Openmarkets taps $22tn tokenised market
items.teaser: Openmarkets Group and Ondo Finance will bring the latter's institutional-grade tokenised financial products to eligible Australian investors, developing new products tailored to the local market.

items.title: Mining, property fuel Aussie billionaires' wealth
items.teaser: Australian billionaires' riches are highly concentrated in mining, financial services, technology and property, accounting for 0.7% of the total US$15.1 trillion in global wealth studied by the 2026 Billionaire Census.

items.title: Natixis IM adds Mirova private assets team in Sydney
items.teaser: Natixis Investment Managers affiliate Mirova has launched a dedicated private assets team in Sydney. The new team will initially consist of three professionals, including Kim Nguyen as an investment director, and an unnamed investment manager and investment analyst.

items.title: FEATURE | Digital advice | Interlocking the pieces
items.teaser: Digital advice has become a core offering for wealth managers, yet it confuses many and implementation and use remain fragmented. Before it can achieve aspirations of scale, experts are urging for a better, unified understanding of the offering.

items.title: GQG Partners sees year of consecutive monthly outflows
items.teaser: Investors are yet to be convinced by GQG’s pivot back into technology with outflows continuing through August. In its monthly funds under management (FUM) update, it saw US$4.3 billion ($6 billion) in outflows during August which is its second-highest monthly outflows since the start of the year.

items.title: Active ETF launches push ETF products past 500
items.teaser: The number of ETFs available in Australia has surpassed 500 after 11 were added in August, according to Betashares. The product volume now stands at a total of 505 ETFs after 11 ETFs were launched during the month.

items.title: Former financial adviser charged with further misconduct charges
items.teaser: A former Sydney financial adviser has been charged with 24 offences of making false or misleading representations to investor and perverting the course of justice.

items.title: Ten Cap looks to AI infrastructure to turn 2026 around
items.teaser: After a turbulent first half of 2026, boutique fund manager Ten Cap is looking to AI infrastructure, healthcare and active stock-picking to drive its next leg of growth.

items.title: Death, incapacity and the auditor’s role
items.teaser: Speaking at the SMSF Association Audit Day, Burrows said there are key objectives SMSF auditors should always be considering and they need to identify where the risks are especially when dealing with death and incapacity as it is then that the risks can be greater.
